findings.title: Spawning `ps` inline during the measured window perturbs the benchmark
findings.message: The runner forks and execs `ps` synchronously when it reads the `grid.perf.ready` record. That is the moment the native process starts the measured scroll samples, so the `ps` spawn competes for CPU on the same machine and can inflate the first measured samples, which feed the p95/p99 targets. The 2-second `ps` timeout also stalls the pipe-reading loop. The measurement-integrity claims in the spec do not account for this perturbation.
findings.suggestion: Take the `ready` observation before the native process is released to measure, for example through a handshake. Alternatively, sample RSS and CPU only at `setup` and `end`, or from a separate thread that is not active during the measured window. Record the sampling cost if it stays inline.

finding.title: Nil render pass used when surface texture is unavailable in measured path
finding.message: BeginRenderPassMeasured returns (nil, acquire, nil) when no surface texture is available. This happens when GetCurrentTextureMeasured yields a nil view without an error, for example when surface acquisition is skipped. drawAllMeasured only checks err, so it goes on to use a nil RenderPassEncoder (rp.End() and the pipeline binds) and will panic. The panic is caught by the new unwind handlers in the trace, but it is still a crash on a diagnostic-only path, and it can leave the surface lock state inconsistent.
finding.suggestion: Return an explicit error from BeginRenderPassMeasured when view == nil && err == nil, for example errors.New("no surface texture available"). Alternatively, have drawAllMeasured check rp == nil and set timing.Failure before returning.
